finalists.label: Chordoma
finalists.why: It has the strongest for evidence, including a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle, curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci, and smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale.

finalists.label: Schwannoma
finalists.why: It has a strong for evidence, including a lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle and compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem, with no against evidence.

frontier_selector.why: The champion, Chordoma, is chosen because it has more specific and unique for evidence, including smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale, which is not shared with the runner-up, Schwannoma.
